summary: Walpole Island Upper A34: a square concrete tower of 1929 on the east side of the South Channel of the St. Clair River, one of a pair set up in 1920; recognized in 2015.

structures.note: Register and Coast Guard list agree on 5.4 m (17.7 ft).

access.note: Offshore beside Walpole Island, a Walpole Island First Nation community. The sources describe no public route to the tower.

events.note: Upper A34 and Lower A32 established as a pair. The original pole lights were later replaced by reinforced-concrete towers, before a major dredging in the mid-1930s.
Recognized as a heritage lighthouse under the Heritage Lighthouse Protection Act, 2015.

evidence.supports: one of a series of lights built for international shipping along the South Channel

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Coast Guard list position (42 37 19.9 N, 082 30 41.5 W) matches the record's OpenStreetMap point (42.622269, -82.511411) to within about 13 m.
The register and the Coast Guard list both give 5.4 m for the structure, so the record's 5.4 m stands.

notes_for_editor: No keeper or storm sources were found for this light. The 1909 Chenal Ecarte range pole lights are not connected to A34 by any source; the story says so. The Marine keepers' table entry for 'Chenal Ecarte range' (P. Willis) belongs to that northern range pair and is not used here. The 1920-21 Ontario new-aids list (garbled OCR) is not cited. The Parks Canada DFHD pages returned no text to the reader; register wording is from HistoricPlaces.ca and Heritage Guide copies. The 1929 build date is the register's; the Marine corpus ends in 1924. Photo: Heritage Guide credits a 1932 Library and Archives Canada photograph (PA-148237, Canada Marine Aids Division); not mirrored. Not used: Wikipedia and Wikidata (record only).
